newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end little changed, eye on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end little changed, eye on jobs data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Wednesday, with a stronger Canadian dollar providing support for the short end, as many investors focused on Canadian and U.S. jobs data out tomorrow and Friday, analysts said.

"Trading has been in a very narrow, stable range. A lack of data this morning contributed to that," said Mary Jane Yule, senior portfolio manager with Jones Heward Investment Counsel. "Things were very quiet. The only positive note was the stability of the dollar."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.10 to C$107.55 to yield 7.345 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 7.08 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 27 basis points from 28 basis points on Tuesday.

Canada's dollar ended stronger at C$1.3853 (US$0.7218) after trading near a two-year low of C$1.3910 (US$0.7189) on Tuesday. The rebound in the currency curbed earlier speculation that the Bank of Canada would have to hike interest rates to defend the currency.
"(The dollar's) stronger levels by the end of the day helped the short end and helped the sentiment a bit," said Yule.

Analysts said investors are now focusing on key Canadian and U.S. employment data being released both tomorrow and Friday. Statistics Canada tomorrow will release its help-wanted index, which will be released at the same time as U.S. inital jobless claims. More complete employment reports will be released in both countries on Friday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.02 to C$101.62 to yield 6.767 percent. The U.S. bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 10 basis points from nine basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.21 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
